crops.recommendation: Use clean, high-quality seeds. Leave enough space between plants so they can grow. Watch closely for small insects like thrips during the first 2 months.
Plant in loose, sandy soil. Add Gypsum powder about 40 days after planting to help the pods grow bigger and have more oil.
Main crop for the rainy season. Keep a small amount of water (about 2 inches) in the field. Use the right amount of fertilizer to get a better harvest.
Best for step-farming (terrace). Use improved local seeds. Make sure the field walls are strong to hold the rainwater.
Plant in fields where water does not stand. Remove weeds early, especially in the first month, so the corn can grow strong.
Good for dry land. Does not need much water. Harvest when most of the grains turn brown.
In areas that flood, use seeds that can survive under water. Plant early in summer to avoid heavy floods during harvest time.
Plant on hills where water flows away easily. Keep shade trees in the garden. Cut back the bushes every 3 years to keep them healthy.
Needs hot and humid weather. Harvest when the flowers start appearing to get the best fiber.
Plant in double rows to save space. Cover the ground to stop weeds from growing and keep the soil moist.
Plant young seedlings (about 3 weeks old). Use Zinc powder to prevent leaves from turning yellow (Khaira disease).
Give the first water 21 days after sowing. Make sure the soil is damp and fine when you plant the seeds.
Gives good yield in this area. Ensure water does not stand in the field, as it can stop the plant from growing.
Plant in deep lines (trenches) to save water. Use healthy pieces of cane with at least 3 buds for planting.
In salty lands near the sea, use special salt-tolerant seeds. Add natural manure before the first rains start.
Trim the young plants so they grow strong. Spray medicine if you see small insects on the flowers.
Add a little salt around the tree once a year to get more coconuts. Keep the area around the tree clean and watered.
Best time to plant is the first two weeks of November. Use a machine to plant directly in the old rice straw to save time and soil.
Basmati rice is very profitable. You can sow seeds directly in the field to save water. Watch out for stem-eating worms.
Needs lots of fertilizer and water. Tie the canes together in August so they don't fall over in the wind.
On high ground, use seeds that don't need much water. Use natural farm manure to help the red soil hold more water.
Water the crop when the flowers start appearing. This is the most important time for the corn to grow.
Plant in the moist soil right after the rice harvest. It helps make the soil healthy for the next crop.
Use sticks to support the plants so the tomatoes don't touch the ground. This keeps them healthy and prevents rot.
A very strong crop that can grow even with little rain. It is very healthy and good for the soil.
Grows best in black soil. Use yellow sticky cards in the field to catch small insects early.
Make sure the soil is loose so the pods can grow easily underground. Avoid letting water stand in the field.
Don't plant too late to avoid worm attacks. Use small traps (pheromone) in the field to check for pests.
Use drip pipes to save water. Cover the ground with old leaves to keep the soil moist and stop weeds.
Treat the seeds before planting to help them grow better. Harvest when the pods turn golden yellow.
Plant in straight lines to make it easier to remove weeds. Use lights at night to catch and kill harmful moths.
Best to grow after the rice harvest. It does not need much water and makes the soil richer.
Treat seeds with medicine to stop the roots from rotting. Keep the soil moist when the flowers are blooming.
Plant in the first half of November. Give the first water 3 weeks after sowing. Use good quality, certified seeds.
Plant when the weather starts getting cool. Watch out for small green insects (aphids) on the leaves.
Needs regular watering when the flowers are growing. Protect the field from birds when the seeds are ripening.
Can grow well even in poor soil. Needs less water than wheat. Good for animal feed and other uses.
The most important crop for this area. It can grow with very little water. Remove extra small plants after 2 weeks so the rest can grow big.
Needs proper watering. Use sprinklers if you have sandy soil to save water. It helps get better quality grain.
A safe crop for dry land. Harvest as soon as it is ready to avoid damage from dry weather.
Short-duration crop. Keep a very thin layer of water in the field after the flowers appear.
Use modern methods to get more yield with less water. Drip irrigation is the best for this crop here.
Grows well in dry areas. Can survive even if it gets very hot. Harvest when the seeds feel hard.
Needs 6 waterings at important times, starting from 3 weeks after planting. Use the right amount of mixed fertilizer.
Plant in deep pits to get a massive harvest. Watch out for worms that eat the top or roots of the cane.
Needs lots of fertilizer to grow fast. Watch out for worms that eat the corn cobs.
Arhar is a main crop. Ensure water does not stand in the field when the plants are small. It helps keep the soil healthy.
Early rice crop. Sow directly in the field. Choose seeds that can grow even if there is less rain early on.
The most important rice crop. Keep water in the field for 10 days after planting the young rice.
Winter rice that gives a high yield. Needs a regular water supply from a pump or well.
The 'Golden Fiber'. Harvest after 4 months to get the strongest fiber for making ropes and bags.
